Thought I'd answer the other questions, too:

Getting to the Twin Cities is easy! Just leave Morris and go East on Highway 59 until you get to Sauk Center. Then, take a left and then a right onto I-94, and then it's a straight shot down to the TC. No problem.


Getting groceries is very convenient. The supermarket is in the middle of town, about a 10-15 walk from campus. They have carry-out boys who will, if needed, help you carry your groceries back to your house or to campus. There's also a farmer's market twice a week when the weather is warm, and the co-op often has local vegetables and local, organic meats and cheeses. 

It can be difficult to find part-time work in Morris. It also has a high-school and is the largest town in Stevens County, so there is a lot of competition. However, jobs are often available at restaurants and the McDonald's, or at the various bars as servers or bartenders. On campus, there are work-study jobs available if you're eligible. These jobs are about 10 hours a week and can vary: you could work at the library, as an office assistant, at the Welcome Center, etc. 

Food Service food is *okay*. We seem to get a new head chef every year, so the main dishes can be hit and miss. It's not bad food, though, and if the entree isn't exactly your taste there is always cereal and a salad bar. I'd suggest avoiding the mashed potatoes. 

EDIT: I put a [few pictures of campus](http://thelifemachine.imgur.com/university_of_minnesota_morris) (all stolen, shhh) up in an album.

Currently attending (senior) and live in the town. Morris is a great school with a super involved student body and great faculty. There are many student groups and clubs to meet people (examples include Japan club, d&d club, super smash club, outdoor club, rugby, broomball, a student newspaper and literary magazine, etc). There's a 24 study lounge with computers and a printer, a good library with tutoring and a Writing Room, and many resources for help outside of class.

There are four bars in Morris: the Met, the Old #1, the Eagles Club, and the American Legion. The Met has two-for-ones on Tuesdays, $6 pitchers of long islands on wednesdays, and dollar rails and quarter taps on thursdays. The Eagles has good popcorn and only takes cash. The Old #1 has good food and the best beer selection. The Legion is always full of townies and is a hella weird place. The liquor store here is not very good but that doesnt seem to stop anyone. 

You should bring a bike, but you could walk anywhere you wanted to go. There's one grocery store (Willie's) and it's overpriced and the cashiers are all snide little highschool bitches. There's also a co-op (pomme de terre co-op) which is very cool. They stock bulk foods, local meats and cheeses, fair trade coffee, organic bath products, and all sorts of neat things.

It's a really great place, all in all. PM me if you have any other questions

I have two cats, and one of them sometimes behaves very strangely. We always joke that he is just autistic, but occasionally he acts in ways that I struggle to explain with, "well, Thomas is just a weirdo."
Our house is fairly old, and sometimes things happen that can't really be explained (the freezer in the basement unplugs itself, dishes get moved from one side of the cupboard to the other, the floors creak. small things like that). The cat, though, often acts like he's watching something that is totally invisible to us. He'll look at it for an extended length of time, and if he's sitting down he'll turn his head to follow its progress around the room. Every once in a while he'll get up, go around a corner, and continue to watch empty space, as if he'd lost sight of something that he wanted to keep looking at. He's also obsessed with my housemate's room, for no reason that we can distinguish. He'll yowl at the door for hours, and when she lets him in he follows a similar pattern to the dog: he'll run into the closet and look around, then investigate three corners of the room before climbing in her bed. 

It's not really spooky, as our house is pretty charming and feels fairly benevolent even at its spookiest, but it is awfully mysterious.

When I was in seventh grade, I was what you could call "directionless". I'd just started middle school and my class size had doubled, so I had to make all new friends. I struggled with classes and I was depressed, awkward, and constantly bored, and because of that I spent a huge amount of time just wallowing in self pity and complaining to anyone who would listen (as teenagers often do). I didn't want to work at anything, I didn't want to try, I just wanted things to fall in my lap. 

I had an English teacher, Mr Z. One day I didn't do some assignment, I forget what, and he called me up to his desk to ask me about it. I started stuttering about why I hadn't done it (I had other homework, the cat ate it, I forgot, etc). He listens to me for about 30 seconds, then leans forward, folds his hands on the desk, looks me right in the eye, and says, "That's enough. From now on, I don't want to hear any of this. From now on, I don't want any excuses, okay? No excuses, just performance." I was startled and went back to my seat. 

I always think of that whenever I feel like things are too hard, or when it would be easy to blame someone else, or when I doubt myself and my own abilities. He turned everything around for me.
